title: Verifying General Liability ($1M/$2M) on Commercial Cleaning Bids: The Facility Manager's Protocol
seoTitle: Verifying General Liability ($1M/$2M) on Commercial Cleaning Bids
metaDescription: Verify janitorial general liability insurance ($1M/$2M ACORD 25 COI, CG 20 10 endorsements) and benchmark $0.07-$0.15/sq ft bids in our Quote Comparator.
excerpt: Collecting a front-page PDF Certificate of Insurance is not enough to protect a commercial property from slip-and-fall lawsuits or chemical damage claims. Learn how US facility managers verify ACORD 25 forms, mandatory ISO additional insured endorsements, and embedded overhead costs per square foot.
quickAnswer: To properly verify janitorial general liability insurance on a commercial cleaning bid, require an ACORD 25 Certificate of Insurance showing at least $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 general aggregate from an AM Best A-VII or higher admitted carrier, paired with attached ISO CG 20 10 (ongoing operations) and CG 20 37 (completed operations) additional insured endorsements. Fully insured commercial contractors typically incorporate 1.8% to 3.2% of gross revenue for general liability premiums into their base pricing of $0.07 to $0.15 per sq ft for mid-sized offices (2,500 to 24,999 sq ft) or $35 to $65 per labor hour.

blocks.text: Why a Front-Page COI PDF Does Not Guarantee General Liability Coverage

Every commercial cleaning Request for Proposal (RFP) specifies that bidders must carry commercial general liability insurance. Yet during post-incident litigation—whether triggered by an executive slipping on a freshly mopped elevator lobby, an overflowing utility slop sink flooding a below-grade server room, or an unapproved high-alkaline stripper ruining custom lobby terrazzo—property managers routinely discover that the one-page ACORD 25 PDF sitting in their vendor file confers zero legal protection to the building owner or tenant.

Printed across the top of every standard ACORD 25 Certificate of Insurance is a legally binding disclaimer stating that the certificate is issued as a matter of information only, confers no rights upon the certificate holder, and does not amend, extend, or alter the coverage afforded by the underlying policies. If a janitorial contractor lists your corporate entity or property management firm in the 'Certificate Holder' box at the bottom left of the page without attaching the actual policy endorsement pages, their insurer has no duty to defend you when a third-party plaintiff names both the cleaning vendor and the building owner in a premises liability lawsuit.

For US commercial office suites ranging from 2,500 to 25,000+ square feet, verifying general liability insurance is both a risk-transfer discipline and a pricing benchmark check. Contractors operating at standard commercial market rates—typically $0.09 to $0.15 per sq ft per visit for 2,500 to 9,999 sq ft suites, or $0.07 to $0.12 per sq ft for 10,000 to 24,999 sq ft properties—carry verifiable ISO commercial general liability (CGL) policies classified under the exact janitorial underwriting payroll codes. Unusually low bids that undercut market averages by 20% or more frequently rely on misclassified artisan policies, lapsed installment policies, or excluded property-damage sublimits.

blocks.title: Mandatory ACORD 25 Verification Rule
blocks.text: Never sign a notice to proceed or hand over building master keys based solely on an ACORD 25 summary sheet. Require the vendor's insurance broker to email the ACORD 25 plus the physical ISO endorsement pages (CG 20 10, CG 20 37, and CG 24 04 Waiver of Subrogation) directly from the brokerage's corporate domain to your procurement address.
Required Coverage Limits and Policy Endorsements by Facility Tier

Commercial real estate leases and institutional asset managers categorize janitorial general liability requirements according to building class, tenant density, and total square footage under management. A standard commercial general liability policy is broken into six core limit lines on the ACORD 25 form, plus umbrella or excess liability layers for higher-risk or multi-tenant properties.

While a single-tenant suburban office under 2,500 sq ft paying the standard minimum per-visit charge of $90 to $135 might accept a baseline $1,000,000 per-occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate structure, Class A high-rise towers and multi-floor corporate headquarters require primary limits paired with a commercial umbrella policy. Furthermore, facility managers must look closely at the 'Damage to Rented Premises' line item—often called Fire Legal Liability—and 'Care, Custody, or Control' (CCC) property damage extensions. Because janitorial crews physically handle tenant property, standard CGL policies sometimes exclude damage to surfaces the cleaner is actively working on unless a Broad Form Property Damage or voluntary property damage endorsement is active.

blocks.text: How General Liability Costs Factor Into Your Monthly Janitorial Quote

Understanding the actuarial math behind a cleaning contractor's insurance expense prevents procurement teams from falling for unsustainable underbidding. Commercial general liability for janitorial services (typically underwritten under ISO Class Code 96816 for commercial cleaning) is priced on gross receipts or audited direct labor payroll. Depending on the contractor's five-year loss run history, state litigation climate, and whether they perform higher-hazard tasks like exterior window washing or high-speed floor burnishing, a legitimate CGL policy with a $2M/$4M limit and umbrella layer costs the vendor between 1.8% and 3.5% of gross contract revenue.

Consider a 15,000-square-foot corporate office with mixed carpet and VCT hard flooring (a 1.05x flooring multiplier) cleaned 5 times per week (21.65 visits per month based on 4.33 weeks per month, applying the 0.90x daily frequency efficiency factor). At a mid-market benchmark rate of $0.085 per sq ft per visit prior to discounts, or an effective monthly contract price around $4,400 to $5,800 depending on restroom density ($15 to $30 per restroom per visit) and breakroom sanitation ($12 to $25 per visit), the contractor's direct general liability premium allocation is roughly $95 to $185 per month. When paired with statutory workers' compensation, commercial auto, and umbrella policies, total insurance overhead accounts for 7% to 11% of the total invoice.

When a bidder submits a quote built on a $24 per hour labor rate instead of the verified US commercial standard of $35 to $65 per hour (or $55 to $95 per hour for specialty scrub-and-recoat floor crews), they frequently achieve that price by declaring only a fraction of their workforce or subbing the account out to uninsured 1099 operators. If an uninsured subcontractor leaves a wet floor without wet-floor cones or leaves chemicals unsecured during daytime service, their non-compliance pierces the prime vendor's coverage.
Step-by-Step Protocol for Auditing a Bidder's General Liability Package

Before awarding a janitorial service agreement, run every finalist through a structured five-step insurance verification workflow. This eliminates forged PDFs, cancelled policies, and dangerous coverage gaps before the crew ever steps onto your floor.

items.name: Step 1: Require Broker-Direct Delivery of the ACORD 25 and Endorsements
items.text: Instruct finalists that you do not accept COI PDFs forwarded by the cleaning company's sales rep. The licensed insurance producer listed in the top-right block of the ACORD 25 must email the certificate directly to your procurement team, including the policy declaration number, effective dates, and producer phone number.

items.name: Step 2: Verify AM Best Financial Strength and Admitted Status
items.text: Check the NAIC number listed next to 'Insurer A' on the ACORD 25 form. Confirm the carrier holds an AM Best rating of A- (Excellent) or better and a financial size category of VII or higher. If the insurer is a Surplus Lines (non-admitted) carrier, verify that the policy does not contain restrictive subcontractor or habitational exclusions.

items.name: Step 3: Inspect Attached ISO Endorsement Forms Line by Line
items.text: Confirm attachment of ISO CG 20 10 (Additional Insured – Owners, Lessees or Contractors – Scheduled Person or Organization) AND ISO CG 20 37 (Additional Insured – Completed Operations). Verify that ISO CG 20 01 (Primary and Non-Contributory) and ISO CG 24 04 (Waiver of Transfer of Rights of Recovery Against Others to Us) are explicitly attached so the janitor's policy pays first without subrogating against your property policy.

items.name: Step 4: Confirm Per-Location Aggregate (ISO CG 25 04)
items.text: If your janitorial vendor services 40 other buildings in your metro area, a single $2,000,000 general aggregate limit could be exhausted by a major slip-and-fall lawsuit at another client's property in March, leaving your building uninsured through December. Require endorsement CG 25 04 (Designated Location(s) General Aggregate Limit) so your building commands its own dedicated $2,000,000 aggregate pool.

items.name: Step 5: Cross-Check Operational Hazard Controls on Site
items.text: Insurance underwriters mandate physical hazard controls to keep premises liability coverage valid. Verify that the vendor stages chemicals in lockable mobile units—such as the Suncast Commercial Housekeeping Cart with Locking Cabinet—and maintains touchless restroom fixtures like the Georgia-Pacific enMotion Impulse 8-Inch Compact Towel Dispenser and Georgia-Pacific Compact Vertical Coreless Toilet Paper Dispenser to reduce water-drip slip hazards and core waste near restroom thresholds.

blocks.text: Connecting Physical Facility Equipment to General Liability Risk Reduction

Insurance verification does not end in the legal department; underwriters and defense attorneys look at on-site physical operating procedures when adjudicating commercial slip-and-fall or chemical exposure claims. Over 65% of commercial janitorial general liability claims stem from two preventable floor hazards: water pooled around restroom handwashing stations and unattended chemical containers in active daytime corridors.

Specifying commercial-grade hardware in your janitorial scope directly curtails these exposures. For example, requiring day porters and evening crews to transport concentrated disinfectants and bowl cleaners inside a Suncast Commercial Housekeeping Cart with Locking Cabinet (featuring locking cabinet doors, a 300 lb weight capacity, and 8-inch quiet-rolling wheels) prevents unauthorized tenant contact or accidental spills in carpeted hallways. Similarly, outfitting office kitchenettes and high-traffic washrooms with the Georgia-Pacific enMotion Impulse 8-Inch Compact Towel Dispenser (touchless dispense with a compact depth profile running on 4 D-cell batteries) and the Georgia-Pacific Compact Vertical Coreless Toilet Paper Dispenser (holding up to 3,000 sheets across dual coreless rolls with an ADA slim profile and keyed lock) minimizes paper litter, floor water tracking, and wet plumbing clogs that trigger third-party water-damage claims.

items: Locking chemical storage on mobile carts: Satisfies OSHA HazCom physical control standards and blocks attractive-nuisance or accidental chemical spill liability in occupied suites.

Touchless paper towel dispensing near sinks: Cuts floor water droplet accumulation by up to 40% compared to loose folded towel stacks, directly lowering ceramic tile slip-and-fall incidence (where ceramic tile & grout already commands a 1.12x labor multiplier).
Coreless keyed-lock tissue dispensers: Eliminates discarded cardboard cores that frequently cause commercial toilet overflows and multi-floor ceiling damage claims.
Documented floor-care chemical compatibility: Prevents voided manufacturer warranties on VCT vinyl (1.04x multiplier) and engineered hardwood (1.08x multiplier).

faqs.q: Why do I need both ISO CG 20 10 and CG 20 37 endorsements on a janitorial general liability policy?
faqs.a: ISO CG 20 10 only covers your building as an Additional Insured while the janitorial crew is actively on site performing ongoing operations (for example, between 6:00 PM and 10:00 PM). Most office slip-and-fall accidents or chemical reaction injuries happen the next morning at 8:30 AM after the cleaners have clocked out and left the premises. That next-morning event falls under 'Completed Operations,' which is only covered if the vendor also attaches the ISO CG 20 37 Completed Operations Additional Insured endorsement.

faqs.q: What is Care, Custody, or Control (CCC) in janitorial general liability insurance?
faqs.a: Standard commercial general liability policies exclude damage to personal property that is in the insured contractor's immediate 'care, custody, or control.' If a cleaner knocks over a $12,000 conference room smart board while dusting it or ruins a 4,000-square-foot hardwood floor while applying an improper stripping chemical, a strict CCC exclusion can allow the insurer to deny the claim. Always verify that the vendor's CGL policy includes a Broad Form Property Damage or Voluntary Property Damage endorsement covering property worked upon up to at least $50,000 to $250,000.

faqs.q: How does cleaning frequency affect a contractor's general liability exposure and monthly pricing?
faqs.a: In commercial janitorial contracts, monthly billing uses the industry standard of 4.33 weeks per month (52 weeks divided by 12 months). A 5x-week daily schedule equals 21.65 visits per month (carrying a 0.90x per-visit efficiency multiplier), whereas a 1x-week schedule equals 4.33 visits per month (carrying a 1.08x multiplier). Because general liability premiums are audited against gross revenue and total payroll hours on site, daily 5x-week accounts with day porters carry higher cumulative premises exposure and require strict Per-Location Aggregate (CG 25 04) limits.

faqs.q: How can I verify that a cleaning vendor didn't cancel their general liability policy two weeks after winning the contract?
faqs.a: Require the vendor's insurance carrier to include a 30-Day Notice of Cancellation endorsement dedicated to the Additional Insured, and schedule an automated mid-term COI verification audit every 6 months. Additionally, have the vendor's broker send updated COIs directly to your compliance inbox 15 days prior to the policy expiration date listed in the 'Policy Exp' column of the ACORD 25 form.

faqs.q: Does a janitorial general liability policy cover employee theft of laptops or office equipment?
faqs.a: No. Commercial general liability only covers accidental third-party bodily injury, property damage, and personal/advertising injury. Intentional acts, including employee theft of tenant laptops, cash, or proprietary hardware, are explicitly excluded from general liability policies and must be covered under a separate Third-Party Employee Dishonesty / Janitorial Surety Bond.
